comparison_with_protocol_2_0.interpretation: Fine-grained exact agreement increased, and binary false positives fell to zero, but item-level recall materially worsened because 10 of 14 human item-level surfaces were missed. The preregistered M4 item-level acceptance guidance is therefore not met.

diagnostic_findings: Protocol 2.1.0 remains highly conservative for item-level detection: it produced no binary false positives but missed 10 of 14 human item-level surfaces.
DFF is the dominant item-level failure cluster: six of seven human audiovisual-item trailer pages were predicted unknown; only one was correctly recognized as audiovisual_item.
Cineam also shows item-level under-detection: three human audiovisual_item pages were predicted unknown, while several non-item navigation surfaces were also unknown.
Czech Television achieved perfect binary item-level discrimination on its eight reviewed units, but fine-grained non-item roles remained confused among homepage, institutional landing and unknown.
Search/index recognition remains weak overall: only 1 of 19 human search_or_index surfaces was classified exactly as search_or_index.
Access-state inference agreed with the human reference on all 36 units, supporting continued separation of access state from semantic surface role.
sample_composition_notes: All six preregistered entities completed collection, but the deterministic global cap of 36 review units yielded no filmarchiv_austria unit in the final review queue. This is treated as a sample-composition limitation under the preregistered cap rather than a protocol deviation.

acceptance_assessment.rationale: Exact multiclass agreement remains low, search/index recall is poor, and binary item-level recall is 28.57%, materially worse than protocol 2.0.0 despite zero false positives.

scientific_decision: Do not accept protocol 2.1.0 as independently validated for fine-grained M3 surface typing and do not scale M4. Preserve the independent result, retain access-state separation, revise item-level detection and search/index resolution in a new protocol version, and require a new preregistered prediction-frozen independent ecological validation before M4 scaling.
limitations: The independent ecological sample contains 36 units from five effective review entities and is too small for broad generalisation.
Although all six preregistered entities completed collection, the deterministic global review cap left filmarchiv_austria without a reviewed unit.
The sample was not designed to estimate prevalence of surface classes.
Homepage and restricted_or_unavailable had zero human support, while several other classes had support of one; performance claims for sparse classes are not generalizable.
Within-entity repetition is substantial, especially the seven DFF trailer pages, so aggregate binary metrics are sensitive to clustered route patterns.
Human labels are authoritative for this blind validation and include deliberately fine semantic judgments that should not be retroactively revised using model output.
prohibited_interpretations: does not estimate corpus-wide prevalence of surface classes
does not validate protocol 2.1.0 for fine-grained surface typing
zero binary false positives does not compensate for the 10 item-level false negatives
does not modify the official T2 baseline
does not establish any institutional or audiovisual-content AI claim
